messages:
tess: Heads up, sample-app CI started failing type checks after the newest python SDK bump. pyright errors on streaming return types and mypy reports fields as Any from generated models.

rahul: Can you paste a short example error?

tess: pyright: Expression of type 'list[Item] | None' is not iterable on `for i in resp.items:`. mypy: 'Item' expected but got 'Any' when constructing list from response parsing.

anya: Probably two issues: the codegen started emitting PEP 604 unions (`list[Foo] | None`) and we ship runtime pydantic models without stubs so static checkers see Any.

rahul: I propose the generator emits .pyi stubs (CLI flag `--emit-pyi`) targeting py3.8 typing (typing.List/Optional) and includes overloads for streaming endpoints. That keeps runtime unchanged and gives type checkers proper defs.

tess: For streaming, overloaded stubs would be ideal. Example pyi pattern: `@overload
def stream(..., parse: bool = False) -> AsyncIterator[bytes]: ...
@overload
def stream(..., parse: bool = True) -> AsyncIterator[EventDelta]: ...`

anya: Also watch forward refs/circular models. Use `from typing import List, Optional, TYPE_CHECKING` and stringified refs like `List["Foo"]` in stubs. Add `py.typed` if we include inline annotations.

types-bot: CI report: pyright check failed in sample-app (branch: tess/emit-pyi) see https://ci.redwood.example/build/1302

rahul: I'll prototype `--emit-pyi` and a small sample-app smoke test running mypy+pyright in CI. If green, add a release checklist item for types smoke test.

tess: Thanks—I'll open a draft PR with the pyi emitter and streaming overloads. cc @anya for formatting rules and @rahul for tests. :thumbsup:
